title: channel_recent read endpoint + context (AdminRepo + explicit tenant filter, since/limit, live-only, oracle-safe)

story.as_a: coding agent starting or resuming work on a repo
story.i_want_to: read the recent, non-expired posts on my repo's channel, optionally only those since a timestamp
story.so_that: I can see what other sessions (on any machine) said or did without anyone hand-relaying it to me

rationale: This is the read half and the payload behind the SessionStart TEAM CHANNEL block. It must be strictly tenant+project scoped (AdminRepo + explicit tenant_id filter, the loopctl content pattern), cheap, return only live posts newest-first with a since delta, and never leak whether another tenant's project exists.

background.includes: Read scoping mirrors ProjectController agent-open, tenant-scoped reads; queried via AdminRepo + explicit tenant_id filter (NOT RLS Repo).

acceptance_criteria.description: GET /api/v1/channel/posts?project_id=&since=&limit= is RequireRole :agent, tenant-scoped from the key, and returns posts for that project_id. Ordering is CONDITIONAL on the delta mode (Coordination.order_recent/2): a DELTA read orders GREATEST(inserted_at, updated_at) DESC, seq DESC — the SAME expression the since filter uses (AC-39.3.3); a NON-DELTA read orders inserted_at DESC, seq DESC. The delta predicate is precisely 'since RESOLVES to a %DateTime{} (via Coordination.normalize_since/1) AND no cursor is present' — NOT merely 'since was supplied': order_recent/2 dispatches on the RESOLVED value (%DateTime{} vs nil), and a malformed or date-only since is present-but-resolves-to-nil, so that read takes the NON-DELTA branch (AC-39.3.3). The delta ordering exists because a keyed slot whose updated_at (not inserted_at) advanced past since MATCHES the filter yet, ordered by its stale inserted_at, would rank last among matched rows and be the FIRST row dropped by LIMIT — precisely the SessionStart working-state slot the bus exists to surface. (Epic 40 later added a keyset cursor OUTSIDE this story's parameter list, making three modes, not two: Coordination.recent_page/3 NULLs since whenever a cursor is present, so ?cursor=&since= is a HISTORY read and takes the non-delta inserted_at DESC, seq DESC clause; see AC-40.C2.4.) seq is the deterministic tie-breaker in both branches: a DB-side bigserial column (added by migration 20260718000000_harden_channel_posts_slot_and_ordering.exs), mapped on Loopctl.Coordination.ChannelPost as field :seq, :integer, read_after_writes: true — Ecto never generates it, it is read back from the sequence. Do NOT unify the two orderings: a re-touched slot is a DELTA concept, not a history concept (consistent with Epic 40 AC-40.C2.4). An OpenApiSpex operation/1 spec is declared (passes openapi_test.exs).
Only LIVE posts are returned: the query filters expires_at > now() defensively (independent of the sweep), so an expired-but-not-yet-swept post never appears.

since (ISO8601) filters to greatest(inserted_at, updated_at) > since (Coordination.apply_since/2) — with the caveat that the caller passes commit_lag_since(since) (Coordination.recent_page/3 via the commit_lag_since/1 helper), which subtracts @commit_lag_epsilon_seconds (= 5), so the EFFECTIVE boundary is > since - 5s: a deliberate at-least-once overlap for commit lag (AC-40.C2.2), so a row touched within 5s BEFORE since is RE-RETURNED, not excluded, and the consumer dedups. limit defaults to @default_recent_limit (25) and is CLAMPED to @max_recent_limit (100) (a larger value is clamped, matching the read-bound convention — not a 400). MALFORMED since IS A NO-OP, NEVER AN ERROR: Coordination.normalize_since/1 resolves an absent, malformed, or date-only (wrong-granularity) value to nil, which makes the filter a no-op AND puts the read on the non-delta branch of order_recent/2 (AC-39.3.1), so the caller gets the NEWEST PAGE. Never a 500, never a 400, never a forced-empty list. An offset-less but otherwise valid ISO8601 instant (e.g. "2026-07-18T00:00:00") IS accepted and interpreted as UTC (Coordination.parse_since/1), because DateTime.from_iso8601/1 rejects it and silently disabling the delta would defeat the 'read only what's new' contract.

ORACLE-SAFE: a project_id belonging to another tenant, or a nonexistent project_id, returns 200 with an EMPTY list — UNIFORMLY, identical to an owned-but-empty project. It NEVER returns 404 and never a different status/body that would reveal whether the project exists in another tenant.

Each returned post includes id, agent_id, session_id, host, key, body, refs, inserted_at, updated_at — enough to render 'who / which machine / which session / when' and to self-dedupe by session_id. agent_id is the only server-stamped (authoritative) attribution; session_id/host are client-supplied and informational.
The response is a standard {data: [...], meta: {...}} envelope; meta carries the applied limit and returned count.
Query uses AdminRepo with an EXPLICIT tenant_id filter (never relies on RLS as the isolation mechanism), consistent with Knowledge/Projects reads.

acceptance_criteria_amendments.original_wording: GET /api/v1/channel/posts?project_id=&since=&limit= is RequireRole :agent, tenant-scoped from the key, and returns posts for that project_id ordered inserted_at DESC. An OpenApiSpex operation/1 spec is declared (passes openapi_test.exs).
acceptance_criteria_amendments.amended_wording: ... returns posts for that project_id with CONDITIONAL ordering: delta (since RESOLVES to a %DateTime{} via normalize_since/1 AND no cursor) orders GREATEST(inserted_at, updated_at) DESC, seq DESC — the same expression the since filter uses; non-delta (no since, a since that resolves to nil, or a cursor present) orders inserted_at DESC, seq DESC.
acceptance_criteria_amendments.rationale: SPEC WAS WRONG, CODE IS RIGHT — no code change. The flat 'ordered inserted_at DESC' wording is correct only for the NON-DELTA branch. As shipped (Coordination.order_recent/2) the delta branch orders by GREATEST(inserted_at, updated_at) DESC, seq DESC, matching the AC-39.3.3 filter. Without that, a keyed working-state slot re-upserted after since matches the filter (its updated_at advanced) but ranks by its stale inserted_at — last among matched rows — and is the FIRST row LIMIT truncates, silently dropping the exact SessionStart slot the bus exists to surface. seq tie-breaks same-microsecond rows deterministically in both branches: a DB-side bigserial (migration 20260718000000_harden_channel_posts_slot_and_ordering.exs) exposed on Loopctl.Coordination.ChannelPost as field :seq, :integer, read_after_writes: true (see the bigserial rationale comment on that field). The delta predicate is 'since RESOLVES to a %DateTime{} AND no cursor', not simply 'since present' — order_recent/2 dispatches on the RESOLVED value, so (a) a malformed or date-only since resolves to nil via normalize_since/1 and takes the non-delta branch (consistent with AC-39.3.3), and (b) Epic 40's keyset cursor (outside this story's parameter list) NULLs since when a cursor is supplied (recent_page/3), so ?cursor=&since= is a HISTORY read on the non-delta clause — three modes, not two. The two orderings are deliberately NOT unified: a re-touched slot is a delta concept, not a history-cursor concept — the same split Epic 40 already documents at us_40.c2.json AC-40.C2.4, kept consistent here.

acceptance_criteria_amendments.original_wording: since (ISO8601) filters to greatest(inserted_at, updated_at) > since; limit defaults to 25 and is CLAMPED to a max of 100 (a larger value is clamped to 100, matching the read-bound convention — not a 400).
acceptance_criteria_amendments.amended_wording: ... plus: a malformed, absent, or date-only since resolves to nil — a NO-OP filter that returns the newest page under the non-delta ordering. Never a 500, never a 400, never a forced-empty list. An offset-less but valid ISO8601 instant is accepted as UTC. The delta boundary is also widened backwards by the bounded commit-lag epsilon (5s), so the effective filter is > since - 5s.
acceptance_criteria_amendments.rationale: DELIBERATE AS-BUILT DECISION, not an unfixed finding — the spec is what was wrong. (#428's proposal, quoted for the record: a malformed since should 'return an empty result or 400, never a 500'.) #428's HARD requirement (never a 500) HOLDS; its 'empty result or 400' wording does not, and the shipped behavior is kept on purpose. since is a delta-read OPTIMIZATION on a FAIL-OPEN SessionStart path: returning the newest page on a bad since is strictly safer for that consumer than a 400, which would blank the TEAM CHANNEL block entirely and give a session less context than it had before. A forced-empty result would be equally wrong — it would look like 'nothing happened on this repo'. Coordination.normalize_since/1 resolves ONCE, so the filter (apply_since/2) and the ordering (order_recent/2) can never disagree about the delta mode — which is also why the delta predicate is 'since RESOLVES to a %DateTime{}', not 'since was supplied' (AC-39.3.1). The one case NOT degraded is an offset-less-but-valid instant: Coordination.parse_since/1 accepts it as UTC because DateTime.from_iso8601/1 rejects it, and silently dropping the filter there would return the whole channel and defeat 'read only what's new'. Also restated for precision: a RESOLVED since is not applied verbatim — the caller widens it by Coordination.commit_lag_since/1 (@commit_lag_epsilon_seconds = 5), so the effective boundary is > since - 5s (at-least-once overlap for commit lag, AC-40.C2.2); a test derived from the literal '> since' would wrongly assert that a row touched at since-3s is excluded, so any since test MUST space its timestamps by more than the epsilon (see the note on TC-39.3.3).

test_cases.name: returns own project's live posts newest-first
since returns only the delta
preconditions: posts at t1 and t3; since=t2
test_cases.note: SPACING CONSTRAINT (AC-39.3.3): the effective boundary is > since - @commit_lag_epsilon_seconds (5s), not > since, so t1/t2/t3 MUST be spaced by MORE than 5 seconds or t1 is legitimately re-returned by the commit-lag overlap and the test fails against correct shipped behavior. Implemented with 100-second spacing — shipped guard: test/loopctl/coordination_test.exs, describe "recent/3 since and limit contract (US-39.3)", test "since filters on GREATEST(inserted_at, updated_at) > since".

test_cases.name: cross-tenant AND nonexistent project both 200 empty (no oracle)
steps: GET with a random nonexistent UUID
expected_results: both 200 with empty data, identical responses

test_cases.name: delta ordering by GREATEST keeps a re-touched slot inside the LIMIT window (#428 regression guard)
preconditions: a keyed slot whose inserted_at PREDATES since but whose updated_at is the most recent touch
two ordinary posts inserted AFTER since but BEFORE the slot's touch
read with since set and limit 2
expected_results: the re-touched slot is returned FIRST (not truncated out by its stale inserted_at)
result is [slot, p2] — the delta branch of order_recent/2, per AC-39.3.1
test_cases.note: Shipped guards (test/loopctl/coordination_test.exs, quoted verbatim so they are greppable): test "delta ORDER BY GREATEST keeps a re-touched slot from being truncated by limit" (describe "recent/3 since and limit contract (US-39.3)"), and for recent_page/3 test "an upserted slot after `since` surfaces (GREATEST) and is not dropped by limit" (describe "recent_page/3 keyset cursor + commit-lag delta (US-40.C2)").

test_cases.name: a malformed since is a NO-OP filter, never an error (AC-39.3.3)
preconditions: one old post and one new post on the channel
expected_results: both return the FULL newest-first page (old and new) — the filter degrades to a no-op
no raise, no 500, no 400, no forced-empty list
test_cases.note: Shipped guards (test/loopctl/coordination_test.exs, describe "recent/3 since and limit contract (US-39.3)", quoted verbatim so they are greppable): test "a malformed since string is a no-op filter (not an error)" and test "a date-only since (wrong granularity) is a no-op filter, returns the whole channel". The CONTRASTING offset-less-but-valid instant case (accepted, NOT degraded) is the sibling test "since accepts an OFFSET-LESS ISO8601 string, interpreted as UTC".

technical_notes: Context: Loopctl.Coordination.recent(tenant_id, project_id, opts) — AdminRepo query filtering tenant_id + project_id + expires_at > now(), limit defaulted/clamped by @default_recent_limit (25) and @max_recent_limit (100).

Ordering is CONDITIONAL (Coordination.order_recent/2, which dispatches on the RESOLVED since — %DateTime{} vs nil): delta (since resolves to a %DateTime{} AND no cursor) => GREATEST(inserted_at, updated_at) DESC, seq DESC, matching the apply_since/2 filter so a re-upserted keyed slot is not truncated out of the LIMIT window by its stale inserted_at; non-delta (no since, a since that resolves to nil, or a cursor present) => inserted_at DESC, seq DESC. seq is the tie-breaker: a DB-side bigserial mapped on Loopctl.Coordination.ChannelPost as field :seq, :integer, read_after_writes: true. Epic 40's cursor NULLs since when present (Coordination.recent_page/3), so cursor+since is a history read. Do NOT unify the branches — same split Epic 40 documents at us_40.c2.json AC-40.C2.4.

Malformed/absent/date-only since => nil => no-op filter AND the non-delta ordering branch => newest page (Coordination.normalize_since/1). Never a 400 or 500: since is a delta optimization on a fail-open SessionStart path. An offset-less but valid ISO8601 instant is parsed as UTC (Coordination.parse_since/1).

CITATION HYGIENE (CLAUDE.md 'write the structure or the pointer'): cite functions by name/arity, indexes and migrations by NAME, and tests by their VERBATIM test string — never by line number. Line spans in this epic and in Epic 40 rotted within days (a 38-line test insertion shifts every ref below it); a function name does not.
Oracle-safety: return {:ok, []} for a project the tenant doesn't own — do NOT branch to :not_found. This keeps cross-tenant existence unobservable and simplifies the consumer.
Do NOT self-dedup server-side — that is the consumer's job (US-39.6).
This GET is NOT covered by require_human_anchor_default_deny_test (it only walks POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) — no allowlist entry needed (correcting the earlier note).
Emit a security-event log on any internal error but never leak cross-tenant existence.
